messages:
Maria: heads-up — ran a quick multiplexing experiment on ap-southeast yesterday. peak tokens/sec collapsed ~12% when we pushed concurrent requests above 1.8k. thinking it's multiplexer hot path + KV cache churn, not pure GPU saturation. anyone else see similar?
Sachin: saw that too on eu-west. pattern: many short chats (avg 40 tokens) + fat tails of 2–3 long requests. batching helped but warmup waste spiked.
Oliver: can you paste the sim numbers? curious about requests/sec vs tokens/sec split.
Maria: sure — quick numbers below. TL;DR: requests rose 22% but tokens/sec only up 8%, headroom reduced.
Maria: ```
region: ap-southeast
fleet: mixed A100/H100
concurrency: 1800 -> 2200
avg_req_tokens: 48
long_tail_95pct: 750 tokens
observed_tokens_per_sec: 420k -> 454k
gpu_utilization: 62% -> 71%
headroom_estimate: 18% -> 6%
```
Jen: hmm that headroom drop is scary. could be eviction/backpressure in the multiplexer queue adding latency and preventing effective packing.
Kai: on Dedicated we've observed similar when prefix cache miss rate > 7%. KV cache eviction is noisy when model mix shifts. we should correlate cache hit rate.
Tara: @Maria can you run the same experiment but force pinning (no multiplexing) on a subset to compare? we need the delta for cost tradeoff.
Maria: scheduling now. I'll run a pinned ray + multiplexed run and post numbers in ~30m.
Sachin: low-cost mitigation thought: tighten batch windows (from 30ms -> 20ms) and limit per-connection concurrency to 4. Might reduce latency for short chats and improve tokens/sec packing.
Oliver: cost numbers please — what's $/gpu-hour delta if we switch to pinned instances for that traffic slice?
Maria: rough: A100 hourly ~ $2.40 equiv, H100 ~ $3.80. Pinning increases required GPUs by ~9% in the sim -> add ~9% * fleet_hours * cost. I'll calc absolute.
Maria: ```
# rough calc (ap-southeast baseline)
baseline_gpu_hours_daily = 240
delta = 240 * 0.09 = 21.6 hours/day
delta_cost_A100 = 21.6 * 2.4 = $51.84/day
```
Jen: that's reasonable if it buys us stable latency and avoids SLA penalties. Also factor in lost prefix cache benefits — pinned might reduce KV cache reuse across tenants.
Kai: another angle: fractional-GPU packing (slice dGPU) with stricter isolation policies. Better utilization but increases tail latency for some long requests. tradeoff depends on SLO mix.
Tara: we need a short decision matrix for product teams: when to prefer pinning vs multiplexing vs fractional packing. can someone draft?
Sachin: I can sketch it. rough columns: workload shape (short vs long), SLA tolerance, cost sensitivity, cache locality.
Oliver: file a ticket to update the capacity forecast sheet with two scenarios: (1) tilt toward pinning for chat-heavy workloads, (2) improve multiplexer thresholds + tighter batching. link ticket here once created.
Maria: filed infra#78941 with the sim outputs and csv attached. added a couple of graphs.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: experiment-isoheadroom (ap-southeast) — start 10:15 UTC, target duration 45m.
Jen: after the run, can we get per-model tokens/sec and tail latency percentiles? that's the decision data product needs.
Maria: yes — I'll post per-model breakdown + heatmap. early note: models with KV-heavy context (embedding+rerank) drove the worst cache churn.
Kai: follow-up: let's add a short sim script to the repo so on-call can reproduce quickly. sample CLI below:
Kai: ```bash
python tools/sim_headroom.py --region ap-southeast --concurrency 2000 --mix "short:0.72,long:0.28" --batch-window-ms 25
```
Sachin: great. if someone can add that to runbook and alert thresholds (cache-miss > 6% && tail-latency p95 > 420ms), we can auto-scale/pin when triggered.
Maria: agreed. next steps: pin-vs-mux comparison results in 30m, Jen will update product decision matrix, Kai will add sim script + alert PR, Oliver will update forecast ticket with cost scenarios.
Jen: thanks all — let's keep this thread for the artifacts. :white_check_mark:
